slides.label: Introduction
slides.narration: A heater near the floor creates a continuous circulation of air.

slides.label: Particle model
slides.narration: Air near the heater gains energy. Its particles move faster and spread out, reducing the density.

slides.label: Convection current
slides.narration: Warmer, less dense air rises while cooler, denser air moves down to replace it.

params.definition: A circulation caused by density differences in a fluid.
params.example: Warm air rises above the heater and cooler air returns near the floor.

slides.label: Retrieval summary
slides.narration: Explain the movement using energy, density and circulation.

params.heading: Pause and recall
points: Expanded air is less dense and rises
Cooler air replaces it and circulation continues
